title: CCA sweep · mission sequence
subtitle: 2024 TTX · counterair sweep and between-pulse pressure
description: Mitchell Institute 2024 tabletop-exercise concepts: three axes of expendable CCA probing defenses, F-22/F-35 follow-on along one axis, and recoverable CCA with F-15EX maintaining pressure between maritime strike pulses (Figures 3–5, pp. 17–18).
assumptions: These are tabletop-exercise planning concepts, not observed combat missions or validated flight tracks.

The report depicts three approach axes and a 3:1 air-to-air/EW CCA mix but does not publish georeferenced tracks or flight headings; map paths, positions, actor quantities and timeline seconds are illustrative.
The report assumed two notional maritime strike pulses per day early in the scenario; playback is not a real-time sortie schedule.
The report's schematic figures are not replicated or presented as operational tactics.

phases.title: TTX force selection and positioning
phases.narrative: Three planning axes and a crewed follow-on element illustrate the published sweep force package.

phases.title: Three-axis expendable CCA probe
phases.narrative: Expendable CCA with a reported 3:1 air-to-air-to-EW mix stimulate defenses along three conceptual axes.

phases.title: Air-defense response
phases.narrative: The TTX concept sought to trigger reactions by PLA fighters and KJ-500; no actual engagements or outcomes are reproduced.

phases.title: F-22/F-35 supported sweep
phases.narrative: A fifth-generation follow-on force approaches behind one CCA axis using reported ISR and airborne battle-management support.

phases.title: Maritime strike-pulse support
phases.narrative: Counterair sweep supports the report's notional bomber/F-35A/F-15EX maritime strike pulse.

phases.title: CCA-1 and F-15EX pressure
phases.narrative: Recoverable CCA-1 screen stand-off F-15EX, with ISR cueing and expendable CCA-5 supporting between-pulse pressure.

phases.title: Next notional pulse
phases.narrative: Replay depicts the recurring concept, not a published timing or route.
